posts.author: Stereofan
posts.content_md: I found the information; it's interference of a plane wave with a spherical one. I was wondering, however, what the result of using circular slits for a stereogram would be.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
That is a cool idea. It would be a little abstract since it would not give proper visual clues, but it would play the images by tilting the plate in any direction.

Think of each slit as viewable to only one eye. You would only get good paralax when you are looking at the center plane however the images would play in any plane.

This would be fun to do with 3-D subjects instead of stereograms. Hmm...

posts.author: Stereofan
posts.content_md: Let's see if you find this as weird as I do: take a hemispherical lens, coat it with film, develop it as a transparency and scatter the object beam through the transparency in successively masked concentric rings of the holographic plate... on second thought, maybe a conical lens would be better.
